requirements.requirement: Encrypted volume provided and mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: cryptsetup was installed, a 2GB backing file was LUKS2-formatted with a keyfile, an xfs filesystem was created on the mapped device, and it was mounted at /srv/secure. Verified by luksDump, mkfs.xfs output, blkid, and mountpoint/df output showing /dev/mapper/srv-secure mounted at /srv/secure with a test marker file readable. No spare block device existed on the single-disk node, so a loop-backed file was a reasonable substitute for a raw device.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: Persistent /etc/crypttab (keyfile-based, nofail) and /etc/fstab (nofail) entries were added and daemon-reload run. A full node reboot was performed: pre-restart boot_id (739c9792...) and healthy mounted state were captured, shutdown -r now was issued and acknowledged before disconnection, polling through connection timeout/reset confirmed the node was down, and post-reboot boot_id (b9476b96...) differed, proving a genuine restart. Immediately after regaining access, with no manual mount/unlock commands issued, systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service and srv-secure.mount were both active, /srv/secure was mounted, and the marker file content matched exactly, demonstrating unattended unlock and mount at boot.

requirements.requirement: Data on the encrypted volume survives a restart cycle
requirements.summary: The marker file written before reboot (hello-encrypted-world) was present with identical content after the reboot and automatic remount, confirming data persistence across the restart.

overall_summary: The executor delivered a LUKS2-encrypted, keyfile-unlocked volume mounted at /srv/secure via crypttab/fstab entries, and directly demonstrated the auto-unlock-at-boot requirement through a full reboot cycle: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot_id proving a genuine reboot, and confirmed automatic unlock, mount, and intact data afterward with no manual steps. All observed evidence is coherent and consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots (boot_id change corroborated independently). Hygiene is clean aside from two small leftover log files.
limitations: The backing store is a loop-mounted file rather than a raw block device, since node1 had no spare disk; this is a reasonable substitution but differs from a dedicated-device LUKS setup.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured; repeated boot reliability was not tested.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands trace directly to setup, verification, or the required restart-evidence protocol; no unrelated troubleshooting mutations or failed/conflicting services were found (after_executor failed-services list is empty and matches before_prepare). Minor unreverted residue: two small log files (/tmp/dnf-cryptsetup.log, /tmp/reboot.log) from the setup script and reboot command were left in /tmp per the lifecycle diff, but these are bounded, low-risk logging artifacts rather than functional residue. The keyfile is stored root-only (mode 400) alongside nofail mount/crypttab options, which is a reasonable and expected tradeoff for unattended auto-unlock rather than a security weakening.
